item.title: What the UN Secretary-General Nominees Reveal About Climate Change
item.description: Despite calls by United Nations member states and far beyond that the next secretary-general must concentrate on peace and security, climate has never left the scene in the race to lead the UN. item.title: South Sudan: UNICEF reaches communities cut off by conflict in Jonglei state
item.description: The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and partners have delivered lifesaving assistance to families in conflict-affected communities in South Sudan’s Jonglei state, many of whom had gone months without humanitarian support.

item.title: Civilians bear the brunt, with deadly US strikes in Iran and thousands displaced in Yemen
item.description: Independent UN human rights investigators called for an immediate cessation of hostilities on Monday following a series of United States airstrikes on Iran in recent weeks that have killed civilians as tensions ripple through the region.

item.title: Countries must increase AI regulation to avoid ‘existential risks’: Türk
item.description: Voluntary self-regulation by companies developing frontier artificial intelligence (AI) is “nowhere near sufficient” to address existing harms and prevent advanced autonomous AI models from circumventing human safeguards, UN human rights chief Volker Türk wrote on Monday.

item.title: IAEA chief underscores commitment to nuclear safety and verification
item.description: The Director General of the UN nuclear watchdog, IAEA, opened its 70th General Conference on Monday in Vienna with a message full of optimism, stressing that despite the many difficulties and tensions the world is witnessing a “common spirit of dedication” which still guides their work.

item.title: Six UN staff killed in Gaza school strike; Lebanon violations mount
item.description: Israeli strikes killed six UN workers and civilians at a school sheltering displaced families in Gaza as needs grow, according to the UN agency for Palestine refugees, UNRWA.

item.title: UN agencies warn humanitarian system in Sudan ‘could collapse’
item.description: UN aid agencies on Monday said they may be forced to scale back humanitarian aid in Sudan – home of the world’s worst hunger and displacement crisis – due to funding shortfalls.

item.title: Money sent home by migrants nearly doubles in a decade
item.description: Migrants sent $728.6 billion home to families in low and middle-income countries in 2025, nearly double the amount recorded a decade earlier, according to a new report from the UN’s International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD).

item.title: Highly persistent toxic waste threatens ‘many, if not all, human rights’
item.description: Poor management of toxic chemicals and hazardous waste threatens “many, if not all, human rights,” the newly appointed independent human rights independent expert on the rising threat told the Human Rights Council on Monday.

item.title: Global Survey Finds Deep Crisis of Trust as Majority Say Economic System Favours the Rich
item.description: An international survey released by Earth4All has found a growing crisis of trust in governments, widespread anger over inequality, and strong public support for major economic reforms, suggesting that many people across the world believe current political and economic systems are failing to serve ordinary citizens.
